author: Mitchell Boatman
title: Thai restaurant cited for storing cooked chicken in raw chicken box - NewsBreak
text:
By Mitchell Boatman ,
19 hours ago Each week, the Ottawa County Department of Public Health releases a round-up of recent safety inspections at restaurants, schools and other facilities.
Adhering to proper safety practices is critical to preventing foodborne illness and promoting public health.
The Sentinel publishes regular reports on “priority” violations — ones that could directly lead to contamination of food or increase the risk of transmitting a foodborne illness, as well as corrective measures taken.
The Sentinel also reports on “priority foundation” violations — ones that could lead to a priority violation. The health department notes “core” violations, but The Sentinel only reports on those if there’s a significant accumulation at a single eatery or the inspection noted more serious violations.
All reports are available at miottawa.org/health/environmental/food-services .
American Legion Post 6 10820 Paw Paw Drive in Holland
Priority:
The facility wasn’t using sanitizer in the three-bay sink. To correct, chlorine sanitizer is now being used. The person cooking on the grill didn't wash their hands after entering the kitchen. To correct, they were made to wash their hands. Applebee's 3134 Beeline Road in Holland
Priority Foundation:
The restaurant doesn’t have chlorine sanitizer test strips for the dishwashing machine Camp ‘89 10910 West Olive Road in Grand Haven
Priority:
A spray bottle of multi-purpose cleaner was labeled as glass cleaner. To correct, the bottle was relabeled. Core:
Unwrapped plastic and tasting spoons were stored in a container with their eating surfaces and handles mixed together Country Sundae 6481 28th Ave. in Hudsonville
Corrections:
Shake mixing equipment is now being cleaned every three hours The handwashing sink is now being used only for handwashing Of note, the eatery demonstrated excellent active managerial control.
Domino’s Pizza 311 N. Seventh St. in Grand Haven
Corrections:
There's now an air gap between the bottom of the sprayer and the ultimate flood rim of the three-compartment sink The dishwashing machine is now dispensing sanitizer properly Don Petrino’s Pizza 12719 Riley St. Suite 20 in Holland
Priority:
Several items, including pizza sauce and alfredo sauce in the glass cooler and meatballs, alfredo sauce and meat sauce in the flip-top cooler were holding at 48-51 degrees. To correct, all foods in question were discarded. Priority Foundation:
Several cans of mushrooms and tomato sauce had large dents. To correct, the cans were discarded. Core:
The glass and flip-top coolers aren't holding foods at 41 degrees or below There was a build up of food debris and discoloration in the microwave above the salad station. To correct, the microwave was cleaned and staff were retrained on cleaning frequency. The Gritzmaker 120 E. Main Ave. in Zeeland
Priority:
Several items, including housemade dressings, were holding past their discard date in the walk-in cooler. To correct, the items were discarded. Employees were seen wiping a food thermometer with a dry rag before and after use. For immediate correction, employees were stopped and made to wash the thermometer. Raw steak was being stored above ready-to-eat foods in the walk-in cooler. To correct, the food was rearranged. There were several instances of employees not washing their hands at the proper times, including after handling raw meat, after leaving and returning to the cookline, and before donning gloves to prepare food. For immediate correction, employees were stopped and made to wash their hands. Priority Foundation:
The handwashing sink in the dish area has no running water Core:
The drain for the handwashing sink in the dish area isn't connected Corrections:
Proper datemarking practices are now being used Employees aren't handling ready-to-eat foods with their bare hands Employees are changing and discarding their gloves at the proper times Havana Grill 12059 Felch St. in Holland
Priority:
Several foods, including soup, salsa, tamales, eggs, pork and cheese, were holding at 46-50 degrees in the flip-top cooler. To correct, the foods were discarded. Employees didn't wash their hands after handling raw meat, then working with ready-to-eat foods. To correct, they were stopped and made to wash their hands. Priority Foundation:
There were no paper towels available at the handwashing sink. To correct, paper towels were provided. This is a repeat violation and qualifies the eatery for a risk control plan. There's no disclosure on the menu about the increased risk of foodborne illness from cooked-to-order or undercooked foods Core:
The flip-top cooler beside the fryer isn't holding foods at the proper temperature Wiping cloths were stored in sanitizer at 200 ppm. To correct, the sanitizer was remade to manufacturer specifications of 50-100 ppm. There's a build up of food debris, stains and discoloration on the walls IHOP 3110 Beeline Road in Holland
Corrections:
All foods are now being held at proper temperatures Indian Trails Camp 1859 Lake Michigan Drive NW in Grand Rapids
Corrections:
The dishwashing machine is now dispensing chlorine sanitizer at 50 ppm There are now chlorine test strips available on site The ice machine has been cleaned The Kirby Grill 2 Washington Ave. in Grand Haven
Corrections:
The restaurant has made extensive changes to cooling methods to ensure all foods are cooled properly Several equipment repair violations were corrected. The bar dishwashing machine is no longer in use and will be replaced; the sanitizer dispenser is working properly; and there is no ice build up in the cooler. The problematic cutting boards have been replaced MillerKnoll 18558 171st St. in Spring Lake
Correction:
A handwashing sink has been installed in the front area near the sandwich station New Holland Pinwheel Kitchen 20 Washington Ave. in Grand Haven
Priority:
Staff indicated items such as tongs, knives and bowls are being cleaned at the end of the night, rather than every four hours as required Core:
The ventilation system above the oven has a build up of grease and debris Boxes of single-use to-go containers and paper food liners were being stored directly on the floor Paolo’s Pizza 29 W. 16th St. in Holland
Corrections:
The restaurant has obtained new quaternary ammonia test strips Rainy Days Cafe 121 N. Beechtree St. in Grand Haven
Corrections:
The exit door has been repaired The self-closing mechanism on the restroom door has been repaired Rock ‘N’ Thai Express 3440 Chicago Drive Suite D in Hudsonville
Priority:
There was cooked chicken being held in a cardboard box that previously held raw chicken. To correct, the meat was recooked to 165 degrees and the boxes were discarded. There was raw beef stored above ready-to-eat foods in the dairy cooler. To correct, the person-in-charge rearranged the cooler. This is a repeat violation and qualifies the restaurant for a risk control plan. Several foods, including yogurt, milk and whipped cream, were holding at 44-45 degrees in the reach-in cooler. To correct, the foods were discarded. Priority Foundation:
Hot curry was sitting on the counter with no cooling methods in place. The dish wasn't being monitored for time or temperature. To correct, the curry was placed in an ice bath to cool. This is a repeat violation and qualifies the restaurant for a risk control plan. The handwashing sink by the dry storage didn’t have paper towels available. To correct, the person-in-charge provided paper towels. The handwashing sink by the dry storage didn’t have hot water available The restaurant didn’t have quaternary ammonia test strips available. For immediate correction, bleach sanitizer, for which the eatery had test strips, was used. A dried jerky product prepared at another restaurant location was being used without necessary variance approval The restaurant is using time-as-control for some foods, but not writing or monitoring the time for all products Core:
There was cream cheese sitting on the counter to thaw. To correct, it was placed in the refrigerator. The reach-in cooler in the tea/bar area wasn't holding foods at the proper temperature Of note, the number of priority and priority foundation violations qualifies the restaurant for a compliance conference.
Russ’ Restaurant 1313 S. Beacon Blvd. in Grand Haven
Core:
The spray arm in the ware washing area has a continuous leak There's a build up of debris on the edges of the outer door of the dishwashing machine The inside of the walk-in cooler is poorly lit Sara’s Pizza 3114 Chicago Drive in Hudsonville
Corrections:
The sanitizer dispenser has been repaired Staybridge Suites 12170 James St. in Holland
Of note, the drain pipe for the kitchen ice machine has fallen below the flood rim of the floor drain Priority Foundation:
The handwashing sink was blocked. To correct, the person-in-charge removed the obstacles. This is a repeat violation cited at three separate inspections, qualifying the hotel for a compliance conference. The facility doesn't have quaternary ammonia test strips. This is a repeat violation, qualifying the facility for a risk control plan. Core:
Boxes of food were stored on the kitchen floor. To correct, the boxes were moved to be at least six inches off the floor. Boxes of single-use items were being stored on the floor of the meeting room. To correct, the boxes were moved to be at least six inches off the floor. Sundae Sundae Golf Golf 631 Lakewood Blvd. in Holland
Corrections:
The person-in-charge demonstrated knowledge on illness policy, food sources, cold-holding and cleaning dishes Employees are now wearing hair restraints Taco Bell 188 Chicago Drive in Jenison
Corrections:
The restrooms have been cleaned Ted’s 14977 W. Cleveland St. in Spring Lake
Of note, the drain line for the large kitchen ice machine has fallen below the flood rim of the floor drain Priority:
Several foods, including mozzarella cheese, cooked rice, cooked carrots, whipped cream, egg rolls, bacon-wrapped pickles and horseradish sauce, were either past their discard date or lacked a date marking. For immediate correction, foods past their dates or with unknown dates were discarded. This is a repeat violation and qualifies the eatery for a risk control plan. Priority Foundation:
The handwashing sink at the bar didn’t produce hot enough water. This is a repeat violation and qualifies the eatery for a risk control plan. Core:
There's a build up of debris on the inside door of the large ice bin and a build up of dust around the fans in the walk-in cooler The lights above the cookline and near the ice bin and dish area aren't working There are wood planks being used to repair the ceiling in the walk-in cooler. This is a repeat violation. Teriyaki Madness 3155 W. Shore Drive Suite 30 in Holland
Corrections:
The person-in-charge understood and could explain staff illness policies Village at Appledorn West 420 Ida Red Parkway in Holland
Priority Foundation:
The facility's quaternary ammonia test strips are old and discolored West Walker Sportsman's Club 599 NW Leonard St. in Grand Rapids
Correction:
The dishwashing machine is now dispensing sanitizer at the proper concentration Windmill Restaurant 28 W. Eighth St. in Holland
Corrections:
The flip-top cooler is now holding foods at the proper temperature and the gaskets have been replaced The inside of the wall-mounted salamander has been cleaned Ziggi’s Coffee 3830 32nd St. Suite 100 in Hudsonville
Priority:
There's a direct connection between the sanitize bin of the three-bay sink and the grease trap, lacking the required air gap The drain pipe for the rinse basin of the three-bay sink has fallen into the floor drain Perfect Inspections The following restaurants, schools and churches had no core, priority foundation or priority violations upon their visit from the health department last week:
Arby’s at 70 68th Ave. in Coopersville Back 40 BBQ at 477 Washington Ave. in Holland Butch’s Beach Burritos at 726 S. Harbor Drive in Grand Haven Culver’s at 5128 Lake Michigan Drive in Allendale Domino’s Pizza at 5164 Lake Michigan Drive in Allendale Halaula Ice Shack at 907 S. Harbor Drive in Grand Haven Jet’s Pizza at 5135 Lake Michigan Drive in Allendale Ottawa Area Center at 10161 96th Ave. in Allendale — Contact reporter Mitchell Boatman at mboatman@hollandsentinel.com .
This article originally appeared on The Holland Sentinel: Thai restaurant cited for storing cooked chicken in raw chicken box
